about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Mar is steady near 81.5-81.7 after Tuesday's gain, which Barchart tied mostly to outside markets rather than fresh cotton demand. Old-crop Mar/May still rests on Texas Plains crop losses; Dec delivery and high-grade certificated stocks remain a risk for longs, so the firmness is not yet a demand signal.
events: Cotton closes Tuesday higher on outside-market help (Barchart)
Mar ~81.5 in early trade, little changed (ICE/Yahoo Finance)
Texas Plains drought trims dryland yields (Farm Progress)

sugar.fundamental: Mar has pushed back above 18c (about 18.1, +2.7% early) on a softer dollar, firmer crude and a steadier real, which reduce the incentive for Brazilian mills to hedge. There is still no new centre-south crush or mix data, so this is a currency and positioning move; the Brazil supply picture has not changed.
events: Raw sugar Mar ~18.13, back above 18c (ICE/Yahoo Finance)
Sugar supported by dollar weakness and firmer crude (Barchart)
Real holds firmer after fiscal plan clears Congress (Bloomberg)

coffee.fundamental: Dec arabica sits near 267.6 and Mar around 259, close to four-month lows. Reports that Brazilian arabica is moving into ICE warehouses, with talk that certified stocks could more than double, go straight at the Dec/Mar deliverability concern that had supported the front; that keeps the stock build as the dominant factor.
events: Brazilian arabica heading to ICE warehouses; certs could more than double (CNN Brasil, Finimize)
Coffee falls as supply concerns ease (Barchart)

cocoa.fundamental: Latest reports point to Ivory Coast port arrivals running slower again, which lifted prices on Tuesday and cuts against the ample-supply story; rising ICE certified stocks are the main offset. No new Ghana COCOBOD news, and the ICCO November quarterly bulletin is not yet out.
events: Cocoa climbs as Ivory Coast shipments decline (Barchart)
EUDR preparations lift European cocoa premiums (Bloomberg)
